summary: This React component displays all blog posts that belong to a specific series. It extracts the series slug from the URL, finds matching posts, looks up series metadata like colors and descriptions, and renders either a styled hero section with post cards or a 'not found' message if the series doesn't exist.

explanations.20: matchPath is Docusaurus's tool for parsing URL patterns — here it's extracting the :slug part from /series/some-slug-here so we know which series the user wants to view.
explanations.24: We're safely extracting the slug from the match result, which could be undefined if the URL doesn't match the expected pattern.
explanations.42: We're filtering all blog posts down to only those that have a series field matching our current slug.
explanations.50: We grab the original series name from the first matching post; if there are no posts (empty list), we fall back to using the slug itself as a placeholder.
explanations.54: If the series has a custom color defined, we're converting that hex color to RGBA format at different opacity levels and storing them as CSS custom properties (CSS variables) that the styles can reference.
explanations.64: We're sorting posts newest-first by converting their date strings to timestamps and subtracting them.
explanations.82: The ?? operator here means 'use the series image if it exists, otherwise use the default fallback image'.
explanations.98: This is a regular HTML anchor tag, not Docusaurus's Link component, because this page is generated statically by a plugin rather than being a standard registered route.
explanations.137: We're rendering each post as a PostCard component, using the post's permalink as the React key so React can efficiently track which items changed.
